sources.title: Solution of macroscopic state equations of Blume-Capel model using nonlinear dynamics concepts
sources.authors: Asaf Tolga Ulgen and Naci Sunel
sources.reviewed: Abstract, introduction and Section 2.1 equations (1a)-(1b), Section 2.2 derivative equation (2), through printed page 55.
sources.finding: The ideal ternary scalar response matches a known spin-1 response after parameter identification. This scalar iteration lacks the present sphere feedback.

sources.authors: T. Tome and S. R. Salinas
sources.reviewed: Publisher abstract only; full PDF access returned 401.
sources.finding: Earlier strange-attractor evidence and positive growth for a two-dimensional spin-1 recursion. No complete equation comparison was possible.

sources.title: Emergence of collective self-oscillations in minimal lattice models with feedback
sources.authors: Dmitry Sinelschikov, Anna Poggialini, Maria Francesca Abbate and Daniele De Martino
sources.reviewed: Abstract and preprint Sections 2.3-2.4, equations (14)-(34), bifurcation discussion through Figure 10 caption. Publisher/institution copy became inaccessible; arXiv text was available.
sources.finding: Feedback spin and softmax chaos is prior art. Reduced q=3 Potts equations give a four-dimensional flow, unlike the displayed three-state discrete normalized map. Nonlinear or return-map equivalence is not excluded.
sources.visual_review_scope: Figure 5 and surrounding text on preprint pages 14-15 visually inspected. Chaotic panels are two-coordinate Poincare sections, not full three-state clouds.

sources.title: Labyrinth Chaos
sources.authors: J. C. Sprott and K. E. Chlouverakis
sources.reviewed: Abstract, cyclic sine-flow equation (1), Sections 2-3 and coexistence discussion; figure captions in text only.
sources.finding: Relevant precedent for spatial loops and coexisting attractors; ThomasLabyrinth is the leading similarity fingerprint among this frozen reference library.
sources.visual_review_scope: Figures 4-9 on printed pages 2100-2102 visually inspected. Figure 8 overlays six coexisting strange attractors; the selected product portraits each use one trajectory.
